bios.Jesmond Gatt: Joined the Central Bank of Malta in 1984; graduated in Mathematics and Computing, University of Malta, 1995. Over 37 years at the Central Bank, holding roles including Chief Officer for retail banking services, currency management and payment systems regulation; part of the team overseeing Malta's euro changeover in 2008. Board member of the FIAU from 2016, Chairman from 2020-2023. CEO of Malta Government Investments before his MFSA appointment. Appointed MFSA Chairman in 2023; received the IFNY Free Enterprise Award in New York, 2025.
bios.Kenneth Farrugia: Certified Public Accountant, fellow of the Malta Institute of Accountants; holds a Bachelor of Accountancy (Hons) and an MA in Business Ethics. Held audit roles in private practice and the public sector. Director General, Internal Audit and Investigations Department (IAID) for nine years to 2017. Director of the FIAU for six years to April 2023, leading major AML/CFT reforms. Appointed MFSA CEO in April 2023, succeeding acting CEO Michelle Mizzi Buontempo. Also serves as Chairman of the FIAU.

bios.Mr Edward Zammit: Chief Executive Officer of Teatru Manoel (Valletta) since June 2024; previously in a senior role there Oct 2017-Aug 2024. Chairman of the ITS Board of Governors, discussing ITS initiatives on quality tourism education and industry connections in an October 2024 interview. bios.Pierre Fenech: Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Tourism Studies (ITS) — his sole government role since April 2025. He is himself an ITS graduate, holding a Diploma in Hospitality Management from the Institute, followed by a B.Com (Hons) in Tourism from the University of Malta and an Executive MBA. He began his career in food and beverage, event and general management roles at establishments including the Bugibba Holiday Complex, The Coastline Hotel and Island Caterers; in 2008 he was appointed Director of Operations and Quality Assurance at Island Caterers, a post he held until November 2012, when he became General Manager of MKIC Ltd, the company running Montekristo Estates on behalf of Island Hotels Group. In March 2015 he was appointed CEO of the Mediterranean Conference Centre (MCC), and later also took on the CEO role at ITS, holding both positions concurrently for years — an arrangement local media dubbed him the tourism sector's "Super CEO" for. In March 2025, Tourism Minister Ian Borg did not renew his MCC contract; Nigel Vella was appointed to succeed him at the MCC from April 2025, and Fenech has continued solely as CEO of ITS since. He has faced two notable controversies: in 2019 he gave Labour MP Rosianne Cutajar a paid consultancy contract later described as a "phantom" job, since she was found to have done little to no work for the payment — a Standards Commissioner probe questioned the ethics of the arrangement but did not find Fenech personally at fault, since the tourism ministry's then permanent secretary, Anthony Gatt, had approved the related expenses (Gatt was subsequently removed from the post); and in 2021 he issued a direct order using ITS funds to architect Gilbert Bartolo, who was the brother of then-Tourism Minister Clayton Bartolo, saying he was not aware of the family relationship at the time.
